issues.t: Ignition switch can shut off engine and disable airbags (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off while driving, often after hitting a bump or bumping the key with your knee. Power steering and power brakes are lost, and the airbags may not deploy in a crash.
issues.why: The ignition switch could slip out of Run into Accessory or Off, especially with a heavy key ring. This is part of GM's large 2014 ignition switch recall. It started with 2006-2007 HHRs and was expanded to 2008-2011 because faulty switches may have been installed as replacement parts.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Key can be removed when ignition is not off (recall)
issues.sym: You can pull the key out while the ignition is still on, and the car may roll away if it is not in Park.
issues.why: A worn or faulty ignition lock cylinder could let the key come out in the wrong position. GM replaced the lock cylinder and keys.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Electric power steering can suddenly cut out (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, usually with a power steering warning message. It is hardest to steer at low speed and when parking.
issues.why: The electric power steering motor on non-turbo HHRs could fail and stop giving assist without warning. GM replaced the motor under recall.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Power steering shuts off on non-recall years
issues.sym: The steering becomes very hard to turn while driving, often with a warning message. It may come back after restarting the car, then fail again.
issues.why: Early HHRs use the same type of electric power steering motor on the steering column, and it fails the same way. These years were not in the recall, and the 2008 HHR has hundreds of NHTSA complaints about it.
issues.next: Grip the wheel firmly and slow down if assist drops out. Have a shop read the steering codes; usually the steering column motor or its sensor must be replaced. Ask a dealer if any goodwill coverage applies.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips, shifts harshly or fails
issues.sym: Slipping, delayed or harsh shifts, jerking, loss of forward gears, or the car stuck in one gear. The fluid may look black or contain metal flakes.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic (4T45-E) can wear internally, and its pressure control solenoid or control module can fail. 2008 and 2009 HHRs have the most reports.
issues.next: Check the fluid and have codes read early. A solenoid or module fault is much cheaper to fix than a worn transmission, so get it diagnosed before it gets worse.

issues.t: Front end clunks over bumps
issues.sym: A clunk, knock or rattle from the front over bumps, potholes and speed bumps, sometimes worse when cold.
issues.why: Worn sway bar links and bushings, struts, and control arm bushings are the usual causes. The noise can be hard to track down, and some owners replace several parts before it stops.
issues.next: Have a shop inspect the sway bar links and bushings first, since they are the cheapest and most common fix, then the struts and control arms.

issues.t: Worn wheel bearing hums or growls
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed and may change when turning. The ABS light may also come on.
issues.why: The front and rear wheel bearing hubs wear out. They are among the most reported repairs on the HHR.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked soon. A badly worn bearing can get loose and affect handling.

issues.t: Worn struts give a bouncy ride
issues.sym: The car bounces or floats over bumps, nose-dives when braking, or there is oil on the strut bodies.
issues.why: Struts and shocks wear out with age and mileage, and they show up often in HHR repair reports.
issues.next: Replace struts in pairs and have an alignment done afterward.

issues.t: Variable valve timing solenoid fault
issues.sym: Check engine light with cam position or timing codes, rough running, stalling or reduced power.
issues.why: The variable valve timing solenoids or cam phasers on the 2.4L engine can stick or fail, often made worse by dirty or low oil.
issues.next: Check the oil level and condition first. A shop can test the solenoids; replacing a solenoid is a modest job, while a cam phaser costs more.

issues.t: Fuel line leak
issues.sym: A strong smell of gasoline around the car, wet spots or drips under the car, or a check engine light for an EVAP leak.
issues.why: The fuel lines under the HHR can leak, often from corrosion in road-salt states.
issues.next: Do not ignore a fuel smell. Park outside away from heat and have the lines inspected right away; replace the damaged section rather than patching it.

issues.t: Inside door handle breaks off
issues.sym: The inside door handle cracks or snaps off, so you can't open the door from inside.
issues.why: The interior handles are chrome-plated plastic and become brittle. Many owners report them breaking on both front doors.
issues.next: Get it fixed promptly, since it affects getting out in an emergency. Aftermarket handles are available, so you may not need a whole door panel.

issues.t: Thermostat sticks, causing poor heat or overheating
issues.sym: The temperature gauge stays low and the heater blows cool, or the engine runs hot.
issues.why: The thermostat can stick open or closed. It is one of the commonly reported HHR repairs.
issues.next: Watch the gauge. If it climbs toward hot, pull over and let the engine cool. Replacing the thermostat is usually quick and inexpensive.

issues.t: Blower fan works on only some speeds or not at all
issues.sym: The fan only works on high, works on some speeds only, or stops blowing.
issues.why: The blower motor or its resistor fails, which shows up often in owner repair reports.
issues.next: A shop can test the resistor and motor. The resistor is the cheaper part and the more common cause when only high speed works.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensor or catalytic converter
issues.sym: Check engine light, possibly with lower fuel economy or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: Oxygen sensors and catalytic converters both appear in HHR repair reports as they age.
issues.next: Have the codes read. An oxygen sensor is a modest repair, but a converter code can be caused by misfires, so fix those first.

issues.t: Windshield wipers stop or move erratically
issues.sym: The wipers stop partway, park in the wrong spot, or stop working.
issues.why: The wiper linkage or motor wears out, and wiper mechanism repairs show up in HHR reports.
issues.next: Have the linkage checked before replacing the motor, since loose linkage joints are common.

issues.t: Rear drum brake wheel cylinder leaks
issues.sym: Brake fluid on the inside of a rear wheel, a soft brake pedal, or the brake fluid level dropping.
issues.why: The rear wheel cylinders inside the drum brakes can leak with age.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes inspected. Brake fluid on the shoes reduces braking, so replace the cylinder and the soaked shoes together.

issues.t: Headlight bulbs burn out often
issues.sym: One headlight goes out, or the bulbs need replacing often.
issues.why: Headlight bulbs appear frequently in HHR owner repair reports.
issues.next: Replace bulbs in pairs, and check the connector for heat damage if they fail often.

issues.t: Car may not be in Park when shifter shows Park (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter is in Park but the car can still roll.
issues.why: The clip that holds the shift cable adjustment may not have been fully engaged, so the transmission might not match the shifter position.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Dash storage bin door may not stay shut (recall)
issues.sym: The storage bin door in the center of the dash can pop open.
issues.why: The bin door may not stay closed in a crash, so it did not meet the federal standard for interior impact protection.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Aftermarket leather seat covers can confuse the airbag sensor (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light may show the airbag off when an adult is sitting there, or on when it should be off.
issues.why: On cars originally built with cloth seats, aftermarket leather covers could upset the passenger sensing system.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.
